about: Krug was founded in Reims in 1843 by Joseph Krug, a German-born wine merchant who set out to make a Champagne of the highest quality every year, whatever the weather, rather than relying on fine vintages alone. Grande Cuvée is the purest expression of that idea, and each release is now numbered: the 170ème Édition is the 170th time the house has built this blend. Krug, part of LVMH since 1999, also issues a “Krug iD” code on every bottle, which tells you the story of that particular edition.

The 170ème Édition is built around the 2014 harvest, a difficult year in which a fruit-fly attack forced careful sorting; Chardonnay came through best. To give the blend structure, the cellar team drew deeply on the house’s library of reserve wines, especially the cold, late 2013 vintage. In all it combines 195 wines from 12 different years, the oldest from 1998, with reserves making up about 45 percent. The blend is 51 percent Pinot Noir, 38 percent Chardonnay and 11 percent Meunier, and it spent about seven years in Krug’s Reims cellars before release.

Krug describes aromas of flowers in bloom, ripe, dried and citrus fruits, marzipan and gingerbread, followed by hazelnut, nougat, barley sugar, almond, brioche and honey on the palate. Antonio Galloni noted an exotic mix of dried orchard fruit, pear, spice and crushed flowers, and Jeb Dunnuck found toasted brioche and lemon curd with the tension to age for another twenty years. The house suggests serving it a little warmer than most Champagne, between 9 and 12 °C.
facts: 195 wines from 12 years (1998–2014), built around 2014; about 45% reserve wines
